tier_1_act_now.title: BJA FY2026 Second Chance Act: Improving Reentry Education and Employment Outcomes
tier_1_act_now.funder: US DOJ, Bureau of Justice Assistance
tier_1_act_now.summary: Directly on mission: reentry services for justice-involved people, with education and employment outcomes. Nonprofit community-based organizations are eligible. The org's NJ recovery court, IDRC, and reentry partnerships are exactly the local infrastructure these solicitations expect applicants to have.
tier_1_act_now.watch_out: Award size (up to $1M) is 3x the org's annual budget. Federal reviewers weigh organizational capacity heavily; a sub-award or partnership role with a larger lead applicant may score better than a solo bid.

tier_1_act_now.title: BJA FY2026 Second Chance Act: Family-Based Substance Use Disorder Treatment Program
tier_1_act_now.funder: US DOJ, Bureau of Justice Assistance
tier_1_act_now.summary: Intersects three of the org's focus areas at once — SUD, family/community resilience, and justice involvement. Same deadline as the reentry education solicitation.
tier_1_act_now.watch_out: Titled a 'Treatment Program'. The org delivers psychoeducation and wraparound support and connects clients to outpatient/IOP treatment rather than providing treatment directly. Confirm whether the NOFO requires the applicant to deliver clinical treatment itself, or accepts a treatment-partner structure.
tier_1_act_now.eligibility_confirmed: State, local, and tribal governments apply under Category 1; NONPROFIT and faith-based organizations apply under Category 2. Confirmed 2026-08-21 - nonprofits have their own applicant lane.
tier_1_act_now.program_scope_narrower_than_assumed: Targets pregnant parents, or parents of minor children, who have a substance use disorder and are under correctional control - in community settings, jail, prison, or as an alternative to incarceration. This is a narrower population than "family services" generally. The org would need to show it serves justice-involved parents of minor children specifically.

tier_1_act_now.title: Empower New Jersey Grant
tier_1_act_now.summary: NJ-statewide, award size proportionate to a $300k-budget org (roughly 17-33% of annual budget), foundation rather than federal so the compliance lift is far lighter than the BJA solicitations. Best effort-to-probability ratio on this list.
tier_1_act_now.watch_out: SCOPE QUESTION raised 2026-08-22. CFNJ's general eligibility is confirmed favourable - any NJ-based 501(c)(3) is encouraged to apply. But search describes CFNJ's empowerment-themed funding as economic empowerment: economic stability, entrepreneurship, workforce development, financial literacy, and access to opportunity. If 'Empower New Jersey' is that program, it is an economic-mobility fund rather than a behavioral health one, and the 20% fit estimate is too high. The reentry-employment angle would be the only credible framing. VERIFY at cfnj.org/find-grants/ before drafting - this has been called the best effort-to-probability item on the list and that claim now rests on an unverified assumption about scope.
tier_1_act_now.eligibility_confirmed: Any 501(c)(3) nonprofit located in New Jersey may apply (CFNJ general guidance).

tier_1_act_now.title: Champions in Action Grant
tier_1_act_now.summary: Flat $50k award, corporate foundation. Typically themed by cause area each cycle — worth checking whether this round's theme covers behavioral health or reentry.
tier_1_act_now.eligibility_confirmed: Operating budget must be between $250,000 and $5,000,000. At $300,000 the org QUALIFIES - just above the floor. Must be an NJ-based nonprofit addressing a specific social concern. Confirmed 2026-08-23.
tier_1_act_now.theme_2026: 'Uplifting Resilient Nonprofits' - organizations adapting and innovating to meet community needs. Broad and favourable; not restricted to a cause area, so the earlier worry that the theme might exclude behavioral health does not apply.
tier_1_act_now.requirement_not_obvious: Applicants must be able to host 1-2 VOLUNTEER PROJECTS for Citizens employees, including at least one SKILLS-BASED project. This is a real operational commitment, not a formality - the org needs a credible plan for what corporate volunteers would actually do. Given the client population's confidentiality needs, a skills-based project (finance, HR, tech, marketing support) is likelier to work than anything client-facing.
tier_1_act_now.award_includes: $50,000 plus volunteer engagement and promotional support.
tier_1_act_now.fit_revised: Raised from 12% to 18% on 2026-08-23: budget eligibility confirmed, theme confirmed broad, NJ focus confirmed. The volunteer requirement is the main remaining risk, and it is operational rather than eligibility.

tier_3_possible_needs_research.title: SNAP Skills, Training, Employment, Program To Success (STEPS)
tier_3_possible_needs_research.funder: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
tier_3_possible_needs_research.note: Near-term LOI. Employment/training for SNAP recipients; overlap with the reentry population is real but the org would need a workforce services track record.
tier_3_possible_needs_research.programmatic_fit: CONFIRMED GOOD. SNAP E&T is explicitly used nationally to support reentry - work experience, job training, and support services such as transportation and tools for people returning from incarceration. The justice-involved population is squarely in scope, and NJDOL is seeking statewide partnerships.
tier_3_possible_needs_research.financing_model_warning: CRITICAL, AND IT MAY BE DISQUALIFYING. The federal SNAP E&T third-party partner model is 50/50: the partner INVESTS ITS OWN NON-FEDERAL FUNDS to deliver services and is then reimbursed up to 50 cents per dollar spent. If NJ SNAP STEPS passes that structure through, this is not a grant that supplies operating money - it requires fronting 100% of costs and recovering half. For a $300k organization with no stated reserves, that is the opposite of what is needed, and a large commitment could be financially dangerous rather than helpful. CONFIRM the exact structure in the FY26 NGO before pursuing.
tier_3_possible_needs_research.amount_discrepancy: This record held "up to $500,000". Search indicates FY26 totals $6,000,000 with each grantee reimbursed up to $1,000,000. Verify in the NGO.
tier_3_possible_needs_research.submission: Letter of Intent is emailed to WFNJ@dol.nj.gov before the date in the NGO Schedule of Submission Dates.
tier_3_possible_needs_research.recommendation: Read the FY26 NGO before anything else. If it carries the 50/50 non-federal investment requirement, this should move to screened-out on financial grounds despite the strong programmatic fit - and the same question should be asked of the other two NJDOL items (Pathways to Recovery, Job Opportunities for Building Success), which come from the same department and may share the structure.

njdol_structural_finding.confirmed_2026_08_25: ALL NJDOL grant funds are distributed on a COST-REIMBURSEMENT basis. Grantees are reimbursed only for actual expenditures already made, claimed through NJDOL's IGX online system. There is no indication of advance payment.
affects: Pathways to Recovery (2027-03-05 LOI, up to $1M)
Pathways to Recovery - Round 2 NGO (2027-03-26 LOI, up to $1M)
Job Opportunities for Building Success (2027-03-04 LOI, up to $1M)
njdol_structural_finding.what_it_means: A $300k organization awarded even a fraction of a $1M NJDOL grant must fund payroll and services from its own resources first and recover the money afterwards. This does not disqualify the org, but it makes working capital - a line of credit, reserves, or a bridge funder - a precondition for accepting an award of any size here, not an afterthought.
njdol_structural_finding.match_requirement_partially_confirmed: Some NJDOL programs carry an explicit 50/50 match (NJDOL up to 50%, grantee minimum 50%), with employer-paid training wages counted toward the grantee share. That was observed on training-type grants. It is NOT established for Pathways to Recovery or SNAP STEPS - yesterday's concern came from the federal SNAP E&T third-party model, and today shows NJDOL does use 50/50 on some programs. Still needs the actual NGO to settle.
njdol_structural_finding.action: Read the FY26 NGO PDFs; both are linked in the SNAP STEPS and Pathways records.
